checks.explanation: A right-to-select statement is printed on page 1, the same page where itemized prices begin, so placement counts as correct.

The includesText for the basic services fee lists arrangements conference, planning, family and clergy consultation, shelter, notices, permits and authorizations, and coordination with cemetery, crematory or third parties.
No other mandatory charge for staff, facilities or overhead appears; only the basic services fee is described as added to arrangements.
The embalming disclosure is on page 1 and the embalming price is on page 1, so they are on the same page.
No text states embalming is needed for direct cremation, immediate burial, or closed-casket service; the disclosure says embalming is not required except in certain special cases.
The alternative-container disclosure is on page 2 and the direct cremation price range is on page 2, so they are on the same page.
Direct cremation is offered with options including a container provided by the purchaser, and no text says a casket is needed for cremation.
Direct cremation is described as including cremation and the list notes cremations are done at its own on-site crematory, with no separate crematory cash-advance charge shown.
Forwarding, receiving, direct cremation and immediate burial each have their own priced lines, and no other offered good or service lacks its own line.
The list contains only itemized charges and the four single-price required items, with no optional combination package offered at one price.
No text asserts that law, a cemetery or a crematory requires purchase of any item; the only related wording is the prescribed choice language.
No text claims that goods or services delay decomposition or protect the body from gravesite substances.
Other printed notices about on-site crematory, insurance assignment and test-document status do not undercut any required statement.
